visual_text: Sydney study: 500 people aged 70 to 90, followed for 1 year
Worry and physical risk don't always match
Almost 4 in 10 had injurious or repeated falls.
Suggested: balance exercise and a talking therapy.
About 1 in 3 had injurious or repeated falls.
'Suggested' help is the researchers' untested proposal; 'general advice' is not from the study. Groups are approximate. People with dementia or Parkinson's disease were not included.
Delbaere et al., BMJ 2010; World Falls Guidelines 2022
alt_text: Grid of worry about falling against measured physical risk, Sydney study of 500 people aged 70 to 90 followed for a year. Matched: low risk, low worry 29 in 100; high risk, high worry 40 in 100. Mismatches: low risk, high worry 11 in 100, almost 4 in 10 had injurious or repeated falls; high risk, low worry 20 in 100, about 1 in 3. Suggested help is the researchers' untested proposal.
design_instructions: Single 4:5 light card. Orange kicker, h1.s with orange em. HTML 2 by 2 grid: column headers (physical risk low, high) above, row header bands (worry high on top, low below). Matched cells (top right, bottom left) mint; mismatch cells white with pale orange diagonal hatch, 4px orange border and orange 'Mismatch' tag; big Montserrat share per cell, then short lines. Grey note below. Data C01-19-a (29, 40, 11, 20 in 100), C01-19-c (almost 4 in 10), C01-19-d (about 1 in 3), C01-19-e, C01-19-g.
